# Environment: ContainedClaude sandbox

<!-- Generated by ContainedClaude {{version}} at every session start from {{clone}}/templates/ and
     .contained/config.ini. Do not edit (read-only inside the sandbox); change the config instead. -->

You run inside the ContainedClaude sandbox (`$CONTAINEDCLAUDE` is `1`; if it isn't, you don't, and none of
this applies). Project folder: `{{project}}`.

## Rules
- **Read**: everything the user can read. Credentials and sockets (`~/.ssh`, `~/.gnupg`, the user's own
  `~/.claude` and `~/.codex`, `gh`/git/cloud credentials, Kerberos tickets, `/run/user/<uid>`, Slurm's socket,
  shell histories) look empty or absent: intended, not an error.
- **Write**: only here (everything else is a read-only file system):
{{write_paths}}
  - `/tmp` (private, in memory, deleted at the end; with `/var/tmp` and `/dev/shm` limited to {{tmp_size}})
- **Login node resources**: this session as a whole gets {{session_mem}} RAM (all processes plus files in
  `/tmp`; a process that exceeds it is killed: `Killed`, exit 137), {{session_cpus}} CPU cores at low priority,
  and {{session_tasks}} processes/threads. The network is shared with everyone: large downloads and uploads,
  like all heavy work, are jobs (`cc-run -- wget ...`), not something you run here.
- **Caches** (pip, uv, npm, Hugging Face, torch, conda packages, matplotlib) go to `.cache/` in the project,
  in sessions and jobs alike (the home folder is read-only). New conda environments must live in the project
  (`conda create -p ./envs/NAME`, not `-n`); use a venv in the project instead of `pip install --user`.
- **Read-only inside the project** (they can run code outside the sandbox later, or define the sandbox), also
  in sub-folders (nested git repositories) if they existed at the start:
{{protect_paths}}
  `git commit` works; `git config` and `git remote add` don't (`.git/config`). Folders holding these files
  (`.git`, `.claude`, ...) can't be renamed or deleted ("Device or resource busy"). If git says
  `unable to unlink` one of them during a checkout, merge or reset, that file kept its old content and may
  show as modified: don't commit it; `git checkout -f BRANCH` or `git reset --hard` gives a clean state.
- **Network shares** are visible only if mounted when the session started:
{{automount}}
  File systems mounted inside the project are read-only.
- **No** `sbatch/srun/squeue/scancel`, `ssh/scp`, `systemd-run`, `crontab`, and **no apptainer on the login
  node** (they print what to use instead). Don't work around this; ask the user.

## Running work: as a job
Heavy computation, anything over about a minute, GPU work, containers and large transfers run as Slurm jobs
via `cc-*`; quick looks (head, grep, small Python) are fine directly. A job runs on a compute node in the **same** sandbox
(same read/write rules), can download, and cannot submit further jobs.

```
cc-run [opts] notebook.ipynb [more.ipynb ...]   # notebooks headless, in order; first failure stops
cc-run [opts] script.py arg1 arg2               # .py (python), .R (Rscript), .sh (bash)
cc-run [opts] -- samtools sort -@ 8 -o out.bam in.bam      # any command
cc-run --image path/to/image.sif -- python train.py        # inside an apptainer image (also docker://...)
cc-run --array 1-96%20 -- bash per_sample.sh    # $SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID is set
cc-run --after 12345,12346 -- python merge.py   # start after both succeeded; cancelled if one fails
                                                # (--after-any: in any case)
cc-run --wait ...                               # submit and block until finished, then print the log tail
cc-wait [--max MIN] JOBID ...                   # block until jobs finished (one call; do not poll in a loop)
cc-jobs [--all]  /  cc-log JOBID [-n 100] [-f]  /  cc-cancel JOBID ...  /  cc-info
cc-cluster                                      # every node's CPUs/memory/GPU shards in use + everyone's jobs
cc-gpu [NODE]                                   # live nvidia-smi on a GPU node (default: the first GPU node)
cc-usage [JOBID ...]                            # what jobs used: peak memory, CPU efficiency (also after cc-wait)
cc-build containers/x/x.def [x.sif]             # build an image as a job (fakeroot; glibc base images only)
cc-pull docker://... out.sif                    # pull an image as a job (both also write x.sif.sha256)
```
Waiting (`cc-wait`, `cc-run --wait`, `cc-log -f`) in the foreground returns after at most 55 minutes with
"still running": run it again to go on.
Options: `--cpus N --mem 16G --time HH:MM:SS --gpu --name NAME --image IMG|none --env K=V --cwd DIR`
(`--env` can't set `PATH`, `LD_*`, `APPTAINER_*`, `SLURM_*`: set those in the job's script).
Defaults: {{cpus}} CPUs, {{mem}}, {{time}}, image `{{default_image}}`, partition {{partition}}.
The cluster is shared with everyone: request what a job needs, not the defaults or the limits, and diagnose before
asking for more (`cc-usage`: what your jobs actually used; `cc-cluster`, `cc-gpu`: what is in use right now).
Limits: {{max_cpus}} CPUs, {{max_mem}}, {{max_time}} per job; {{max_jobs}} queued/running jobs (each array task
counts); at a time {{max_gpu_jobs}} GPU jobs ({{gpu_gres}}), {{max_total_cpus}} CPUs, {{max_total_mem}} memory
(an array throttled with `%N` counts as N jobs: throttle large GPU or memory-heavy arrays).

Details: logs in `.contained/logs/<name>_<jobid>.out`; executed notebooks in `{{executed_dir}}/`. In a job,
`HOME` is an empty temporary folder (`/tmp/home`; the real home stays readable at its path) and `/tmp` is the
node's local disk, deleted at the end. Without an image a job runs on the node's OS (same programs as here,
plus apptainer; Snakemake/Nextflow work with their local executor, not their Slurm executors). Inside images
these folders are visible (read-only unless writable above):
{{image_binds}}
Image cache: `{{apptainer_cache}}`.

## Other tools
- **The same instructions for many texts** (summarise, classify, extract): `cc-ask-batch [--model
  haiku|sonnet|opus] [--effort high] [--schema S.json] [--no-cache] PROMPT_FILE TASKS.csv` (columns `text`, `out`), one model call per row
  without tools, the shared prompt read from the cache; one text: `cc-ask PROMPT_FILE TEXT_FILE OUT_FILE`
  (`cc-ask --help`).

## When something is blocked: tell the user the fix (they do it outside the sandbox)
- **Need to write somewhere else** (a results or data folder): `containedclaude add-write {{project}} FOLDER`
  makes FOLDER writable from the next session on. Same rules as the project: below their own home or the
  allowed SDS folders, not another user's project. Until then, write into the project.
- **A folder or share is missing**: `automount` in `.contained/config.ini`.
- **The SDS answers `Permission denied` although it worked before**: the user's Kerberos ticket expired; they
  run `kinit` (outside) and access returns, for jobs too.
- **A read-only file must change** (`.git/config`, `.vscode`, `.envrc`, ...): they edit it.
- **A job needs more than the limits above**: `[jobs]` in `.contained/config.ini` (`max_cpus`, `max_mem`,
  `max_time`, `max_jobs`, `max_gpu_jobs`, `max_total_*`); also `partition`, `default_image`, and
  `extra_sbatch` for Slurm options every job of this project should get (one per line, e.g. nodes to avoid).
- **More memory, CPUs or `/tmp` in this session**: `session_mem`, `session_cpus`, `tmp_size` there; usually a
  job is the better fix.
- **Claude settings, plugins, MCP servers**: `containedclaude admin` (Codex's: `containedclaude admin codex`). Your config (`{{claude_config}}`,
  shared by all contained projects) is read-only here except memory, transcripts and login (`/login` works).
- **Credentials** (private repositories, EGA, servers): hidden on purpose. The user downloads or pushes
  themselves, or puts a credential meant for this project into the project folder.
